physicalNotes: Radius 1.29 Jupiter radii from Bonomo et al. 2015 (2015A&A...575A..85B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...575A..85B/abstract): 92,224.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.56 Jupiter masses (Bonomo et al. 2015, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2015A&A...575A..85B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...575A..85B/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Holczer et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..225....9H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOLCZER_ET_AL__2016): P 1.85555757 d

sources.eccentricity: Bonomo et al. 2015 (2015A&A...575A..85B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BONOMO_ET_AL__2015): e 0
sources.phase: Holczer et al. 2016 (2016ApJS..225....9H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOLCZER_ET_AL__2016): transit mid-time 2454964.6145 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
